title: opalshore-integration-call-raw-notes
content:
Context:
OpalShore Logistics — initial infra + dev intake. Use-case: real-time route summarization + exception triage for last-mile deliveries. Low-latency requirement (95p < 120ms) for short prompts (average 60 tokens). Hard constraint: PHI-lite customer contact data, must run in VPC or on-prem. They are evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) vs Private appliance (on-prem VM/GPU rack).

Attendees:
- Tom Reddy (OpalShore, Platform Lead)
- Leila Ahmad (OpalShore, ML Eng)
- Priya Malhotra (OpalShore, SecOps)
- Aisha Patel (Redwood, SE - owner)
- Marco Delgado (Redwood, infra eng)
- Sofia Chen (Redwood, solutions)

High-level notes / requirements:
- Throughput target: 120 reqs/sec sustained per region, typical prompt size 40–80 tokens, average response 80 tokens.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 120ms (soft target), p99 < 350ms (must-have for SLA conversation).
- Availability: need multi-AZ within their cloud account; prefer active/active across two regions for disaster tolerance.
- Data residency: primary region = eu-west-1. No logs leave the VPC; customer will ingest audit logs to their SIEM.
- KMS: they require KMS integration with HSM-backed keys for model prompts and customer PII encryption at rest.
- Model policy: want Redwood to host open Llama-3-7B-ish variant or Redwood-verified, but are open to quantized 4-bit for cost. Need output parity checks.
- Canary / rollouts: want staged rollout and easy rollback to previous model version (A/B and canary).

Infra gotchas surfaced on call:
- VPC peering + shared services: they have an existing pentagon of services behind NACL rules that drop fragmented UDP; we flagged that model-serving KV cache and gRPC layer expect MTU ~1500 and tolerate packet sizes >1200. Action: verify MTU and fragmentation settings before dataset sync.
- Network egress rules: OpalShore restricts egress to a fixed allowlist; we need to provide exact endpoint FQDNs/IP ranges for Private control plane callbacks and health checks.
- Kube vs VM preference: their infra team prefers VM-based appliance for predictable NUMA/GPU affinity (less noisy-neighbor variability). We should present benchmark differences (H100 vs A100 vs A10G) for their payload size.
- Cold starts for model variants: autoscaling policy must pre-warm KV caches for common prompt prefixes (route update templates). Otherwise p95 will spike.

Security / compliance notes:
- Priya: must have audit trail for prompt inputs, truncated hash-of-prompt storage; no raw prompt logs outside their VPC. We discussed in-proxy hashing + local-only storage and Redwood's optional in-flight masking.
- Authentication: they will use Okta SAML + SCIM; need to confirm Redwood Private supports SSO for the control plane and local operator roles.

Technical follow-ups requested by customer:
1) Exact outbound IP ranges / FQDNs used by Redwood control plane and model telemetry (for egress allowlist).
2) Appliance sizing guidance for 120 req/s: recommended GPU configs and expected tokens/sec for each model family (include quantized and unquantized numbers).
3) Example canary config (policy example: 10% traffic to canary for 30m, automated rollback on >1.5x error rate or >20% latency increase).
4) KV cache warmup strategy and recommended prefix cache population approach for their templated prompts.
5) KMS/HSM integration steps and certs required for their security review.

Initial risk/concerns (internal):
- If they insist on strict egress allowlist + zero external logging, we may need an air-gapped control plane or an ops runbook that ships periodic telemetry via customer-managed collectors. Need legal sign-off for limited telemetry retention.
- Their preference for VM appliances increases operational complexity for Redwood in the short term; may require rework of deployment automation (Ansible/packer images) for on-prem images.

Quick perf back-of-envelope (to share):
- Model family: Llama-3-7B quant-4 -> expected throughput approx 200 tokens/sec per A10G-equivalent; H100 will be ~3–4x depending on kernel selection and sequence length.
- Batch sizing: for p95 under 120ms target, recommend batch sizes 1–8 depending on interarrival; continuous batching with latency budget set to 30ms gives best cost/latency tradeoff.

Decisions made on call:
- OpalShore to trial Redwood Private VPC deployment first (no on-prem appliance yet).
- They agreed to a short POC: 2-week smoke test in eu-west-1 using a single AZ, then expand to multi-AZ if stable.
- Redwood to provide a pre-configured VPC template and a list of endpoints for egress allowlisting.

Action items (owner - due):
- Aisha: send VPC template + minimal endpoint list (due 2026-01-20) -> DONE 2026-01-18.
- Marco: produce appliance vs VM perf delta doc + suggested GPU SKU list (due 2026-01-22).
- Sofia: draft canary policy snippets and rollback playbook (due 2026-01-25).
- Priya (OpalShore): supply sample anonymized prompt set (~500 examples) for parity testing (due 2026-01-28).
- Security sync: schedule joint security review with Redwood security (Priya + Redwood Sec) — tentative 2026-02-03.

Notes after call / running log:
- 2026-01-18: sent VPC template. Included an alternate template with “control-plane pull-only” mode to minimize outbound connections.
- 2026-01-21: Marco shared early perf doc: shows H100 (SXM) baseline ~600–800 tokens/sec for 7B model at seq=128, A10G ~180–220 tokens/sec. Need to validate with our runtime kernels for quant-4.
- 2026-01-23: OpalShore provided anonymized prompts (redacted). Observations: 35% of prompts start with same 3-token prefix (customer-id marker) — good candidate for prefix caching.
- 2026-01-29: Security review scheduled; customer asked about field-level encryption for outbound telemetry.

Open questions for product/runtime teams:
- Can we support a control-plane mode that is strictly pull-only (no inbound webhooks) and provides a signed state bundle to the appliance? If not, need to document tradeoffs.
- How deterministic is model output between quant-4 and fp16 for the Llama-3-7B variant? Need evaluation harness to compute BLEU/ROUGE/diff metrics on the sample set.
- What are the current kernel-level assumptions about MTU/fragmentation in our gRPC transport? Who owns the network-level testing checklist?

Suggested POC success criteria (to align with customer):
- Functional: 98% of prompts processed without manual intervention; output pass-rate >= 95% on parity tests vs baseline model.
- Performance: p95 latency <= 140ms for majority of traffic during business hours; no p99 spikes over 450ms for longer tails.
- Security: no raw prompt persistence outside VPC; KMS-backed keys in place; audit logs delivered to customer's SIEM.

Misc notes / friction points to watch:
- Operator UX: customer will want simple toggles in console to turn on KV cache warming, pre-warm pools, and to pin model variants. Our current console exposes these but UX is buried under advanced settings — may need quickstart doc.
- Cost sensitivity: OpalShore asked for per-10k-token pricing estimates for dedicated reserve vs pay-as-you-go hosted. Need compare tables.

Next immediate steps (this week):
- Aisha: schedule security sync (send meeting invite) -> DONE 2026-01-20.
- Marco & eng-runtime: validate MTU assumptions and run a synthetic fragmentation test in dev to reproduce gRPC issues -> owner Marco (due 2026-02-02).
- Sofia: prepare short POC runbook (4–6 pages) with config checklist, KV warmup instructions, and canary example -> due 2026-01-27.

Contact quick refs:
- OpalShore Slack: #opalshore-platform (they asked to be added)
- Tom Reddy email: tom.reddy@opalshore.com

Personal notes (for SE handoff):
- Emphasize prefix caching in kickoff; show quick demo of cache population via 1) list-of-prefixes upload and 2) warmup REST API.
- Prepare short comparison slide: VM appliance pros/cons (NUMA control, no noisy neighbors) vs containerized nodes (autoscaling, easier upgrades).
- Flag legal about telemetry: propose a minimal telemetry contract for POC (latency/error counts only, no raw tokens).

Revision history:
- 2026-03-05: appended follow-up about canary policy tweaks and added perf numbers from internal run (H100 quant-4 numbers updated).

---- end of notes ----
